# Brainstorm: The Yantra App and the Drshya Design System

> **Companion doc** to [`brainstorm.md`](./brainstorm.md) (platform),
> [`browser_automation_brainstorm.md`](./browser_automation_brainstorm.md) (runtime) and

## Why this session exists

The original platform brainstorm (Sessions 1–2, May 2026) planned a thin localhost webapp —
"one box, one feed, no settings page" — served by a daemon over WebSocket + JSON-RPC. That app was
never built. Per user direction the MVP ran the executor inline in the CLI (`plan.md`: "No daemon,
no WebSocket+JSON-RPC transport, no webapp"), and the only daemon that exists is the FEAT-021
scheduler (`yantra daemon start|stop|status`, single-instance lock, same inline executor).

Since then the CLI has grown to roughly 30 top-level commands and 98 registered options, and
its runs produce a rich, durable record: attributed Briefs with condition statuses and
cited rows (FEAT-053), task contracts with revisions (FEAT-052), honest outcome words
(FEAT-054), run health (FEAT-048), tool-call and runtime logs, verified action evidence `A<n>`
(FEAT-060), saved captures (FEAT-058), confirmation requests (FEAT-019), report templates,
schedules, site ranking and a managed browser lifecycle (FEAT-043–047). A "single box and feed"
can no longer represent this product.

The user's brief for this session:

- A beautiful yet capable UI that speaks for Yantra's futuristic vision.
- Not boilerplate and not "another AI-generated design". Yantra gets its **own design library**,
  built on open source (Tailwind CSS), modular, easy to modify, and following sound design and
  software-engineering principles.
- **Non-negotiable:** the UI supports all current and future Yantra features.
- Seed design language: gray shades (white → fog → black), saturated color for things that
  matter (buttons, icons), Lucide-style iconography, transparent/glassy surfaces.

Decisions taken in this session (user-confirmed, 2026-11-02):

| Decision                | Choice                                                                                 |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Accent direction        | **Ion** — the cold cyan of a heads-up display                                          |
| App shell               | **Chrome app window** opened by `yantra ui`, served by the `yantra daemon`             |
| Headless component base | **React Aria Components**                                                              |
| Where this lives        | This companion doc plus a Session 5 entry in `brainstorm.md`                           |
| Design system name      | **Drshya** (दृश्य, _dṛśya_: "that which is seen" — paired with _yantra_, "instrument") |

---

## Vision Statement

Yantra's app is **a glass cockpit for the web**. Yantra drives a real browser; the app shows that
browser live, with instrument panels floating over it: what the agent understood (the task
contract), what the engine did (tool calls and verified actions), what it proved (requirements
met, with citations), and what needs you (a guarded switch for anything irreversible). Behind
the cockpit sits **Drshya**, Yantra's own design system: a fog-gray palette that saves saturated
color for meaning, three typographic voices for human, agent and engine, and components
that exist nowhere else because they render Yantra's own protocol. The app stays level with the
CLI **by construction**: commands, options and events come from one registry and one
protocol, so a new feature shows up in the app the day it ships in the terminal.

## Problem Statement

Today everything Yantra knows is reachable only through a terminal:

- **Live runs are lines on stderr.** Goal echo, contract echo, progress checkpoints, recovery
  steers and capability gaps (FEAT-048/052/058/059) scroll past; budgets, contract progress and
  the page the engine is touching are invisible while a run is in flight.
- **Evidence is spread across files.** A Brief is `brief.md`/`brief.html`; its proof lives in
  `contract.json`, `run-health.json`, `tool-calls.jsonl`, `runtime.jsonl` and `captures/`.
  Verifying one claim means opening four files. `yantra audit` helps, but it is still text.
- **Consent needs a terminal.** A scheduled run that parks on a `requires_confirmation` step
  waits for `yantra confirm` in a shell.
- **Settings are three stores.** `config.yaml` (installation), `profile.yaml` (preferences) and
  the OS keychain (credentials) — correct by design (memory: one owner per key), but opaque to
  anyone not reading the docs.
- **Priya cannot use Yantra at all.** The secondary persona never opens a terminal.

Two failure modes threaten any UI built to fix this:

1. **Generic look.** The default 2026 path — shadcn/ui components, a chat-bubble layout, a
   purple-to-blue gradient, a sparkle icon for "AI" — would present Yantra as one more chatbot.
   Yantra is the opposite: a contract, an engine and evidence.
2. **Parity drift.** The CLI shipped about sixty features in six months. A UI built screen by
   screen will fall behind within weeks, and the gap shows up as features the app cannot show,
   or worse, controls that do nothing or behave differently from their CLI flag.

## Core Goals

- **Parity by construction.** Every CLI command and subcommand maps to an app surface or a
  reviewed, written exemption; every protocol event kind maps to an instrument or the generic
  inspector. _Verifiable: a parity test enumerates the command registry and the event union and
  fails the build on any unmapped entry; zero unmapped entries at every merge._
- **Evidence within reach.** Any claim or requirement in a Brief opens its quoted evidence in one
  click; any URL opens its attestation chain (FEAT-051 provenance) in two. _Verifiable: e2e
  test walks every cited claim in the golden Briefs._
- **Legible glass.** Text on glass meets WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1) against the worst-case backdrop,
  and Solid mode is always one toggle away. _Verifiable: screenshot-sampling contrast test over
  light, dark and busy backdrops in both themes._
- **Live and fast.** Event latency daemon → app p95 < 150 ms; live viewport ≥ 5 fps while
  keeping the app's main thread under 15% of one core; every local interaction responds in
  < 100 ms. _Verifiable: perf harness on a recorded run replayed through the daemon._
- **Secure localhost.** No endpoint answers without a session from `yantra ui`; Host and Origin
  are checked on every request and WebSocket upgrade; secret values never travel toward the
  app. _Verifiable: security suite covering missing token, foreign Origin, rebinding Host header,
  cross-site form POST, and a canary secret scanned across every response._
- **Own the look.** No raw palette utilities or hex values in components; no shadcn styles; every
  component lives in Drshya with gallery coverage in both themes and both densities. _Verifiable:
  lint rule plus visual-regression snapshots per instrument._
- **Both personas.** Ralph reaches every action from the keyboard (command palette); Priya runs a
  first task within two minutes of `yantra ui` on a configured install. _Verifiable: palette
  coverage test over the registry; dogfooding pass with a non-terminal user._
- **Agent-optional, still.** The app is fully usable with `LLM_PROVIDER=none`: `ask` and
  `research` run deterministically, `do` is visibly unavailable with the reason and the fix,
  workflows replay. _Verifiable: the app e2e suite runs in the existing `--no-llm` CI dimension._

## Target Users

### Primary Persona — "Ralph the Power User" (unchanged from `brainstorm.md`)

- **Who**: Technically competent knowledge worker who already lives in the CLI.
- **Context**: Runs `research` and `do` daily, maintains a handful of saved workflows and
  schedules, reads audits when a run surprises him.
- **Current Solution**: The CLI plus a text editor on the run directory.
- **Pain Points**: Cannot watch a run's contract and budgets together; correlating `tool-calls.jsonl`
  with the Brief is manual; approving a parked scheduled run means finding a terminal.
- **Success Metric**: Keeps the app open beside his work, launches from the palette with CLI
  syntax, and never opens a JSONL file to answer "why did it do that?".

### Secondary Persona — "Priya the Casual User" (unchanged)

- **Who**: Comfortable with apps, never opens a terminal.
- **Context**: Asks questions and occasionally hands Yantra a form-filling or comparison task.
- **Current Solution**: None — Yantra is CLI-only.
- **Pain Points**: Everything.
- **Success Metric**: Types a goal, watches it work, reads a Brief she trusts because every
  line shows its source, approves the one step that needs her.

### New — "The Reviewer" (Ralph or Priya, later)

- **Who**: The same user returning to a finished run days later, or someone they share a run with.
- **Context**: "What did it actually do, and why should I believe the result?"
- **Success Metric**: The Audit surface answers that without the CLI: trust narrative,
  provenance chains, what the model saw versus what stayed local.

## Prior Art & Competitive Landscape

| Product / Pattern                                                                          | What It Does Well                                                  | Where It Falls Short                                                                                              | Drshya / Yantra Differentiation                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Linear**                                                                                 | Keyboard-first, command palette, restrained color, perceived speed | A generic work-tracking vocabulary; no notion of evidence or live machinery                                       | Same keyboard discipline, plus domain instruments (contract ring, evidence pane) and a palette that accepts CLI syntax                         |
| **Raycast**                                                                                | Palette as the primary surface; fast, extensible                   | A launcher, not a workspace for long-running work                                                                 | Palette is one entry point among surfaces; every result has a CLI twin                                                                         |
| **Warp**                                                                                   | Brings structure (blocks) to terminal output                       | Still a terminal; structure ends where text ends                                                                  | CLI and app are twins over one command registry and one event protocol                                                                         |
| **Browser-agent live views** (OpenAI agent mode, Browser-Use cloud, Browserbase Live View) | Show the browser while an agent works                              | Chat-centric; the live view is a video box beside a chat thread; no contract, no proof, consent as a chat message | HUD panels over the live browser carrying contract, engine log and budgets; consent as a guarded switch; viewport blanked on protected screens |
| **Perplexity / ChatGPT deep research**                                                     | Cited long-form answers                                            | Citations are footnotes; no condition statuses; "violated" and "unverified" do not exist                          | Briefs show verified / violated / unverified per condition, cited rows, and a quoted-evidence pane                                             |
| **Apple Liquid Glass** (iOS/macOS 26)                                                      | Made translucency mainstream again; strong sense of layering       | Public legibility backlash; Apple added a "Tinted" control in 26.1 to tone it down                                | Glass is for controls only; content sits on solid paper; Solid mode is a first-class preference                                                |
| **shadcn/ui and generated apps (v0, etc.)**                                                | Excellent ownership model: component code lives in your repo       | Its look has become the visual signature of generated apps                                                        | Borrow only the ownership model; Drshya's visual layer is entirely Yantra's own                                                                |
| **Grafana / Datadog**                                                                      | Dense telemetry, mature charting                                   | KPI-tile dashboards out of context                                                                                | Budgets and health shown inside the run they describe, never as a tile wall                                                                    |

**Landscape analysis.** Every agent product with a live browser view frames it as a chat with a
video attached. Nobody presents the agent's _understanding_ (the contract), the engine's _actions_
(verified, numbered, attributable) and the user's _authority_ (consent that cannot be forged) as
separate, legible instruments, because nobody else has those as separate protocol objects.
Yantra does: `contract.json`, `A<n>` action evidence, `ConfirmationRequest` with a closed
`decided_by` union. Drshya is the visual expression of that architecture, which is why it can
look like nothing else without being decorative.

The timing is right for three reasons: Tailwind v4's CSS-first `@theme` makes a token-driven
design system a CSS file rather than a JS config; React Aria Components gives a complete,
accessible, unstyled primitive layer (tables, trees, drag and drop, date pickers) that we can
dress entirely in our own language; and the UI only has to run in evergreen Chromium (it opens in
the Chrome Yantra already manages), so OKLCH, `backdrop-filter`, container queries, the Popover
API and View Transitions are all available without fallbacks.

## Design Language: Drshya

### Concept: a glass cockpit over a live browser

Yantra is an instrument, so the app borrows from instruments — aviation glass cockpits,
oscilloscopes, survey equipment — not from chat apps or SaaS dashboards. The defining screen
(**Mission**) streams the task browser full-bleed and floats four glass panels over it:

- **Top bar** — the Bindu (engine state), mode, goal, elapsed time, budget gauges, Stop.
- **Understood** (left) — the task contract in the agent's voice, a segmented ring with one
  segment per requirement, and the requirement list with status glyphs and citation numbers.
- **Engine** (right) — the live tool-call log in mono, newest at the bottom, steers and
  escalations marked, the current call highlighted.
- **Command** (bottom) — the CLI twin of the running task, with Copy, and the palette shortcut.

The element the engine is touching gets **target brackets** (four corner ticks) labelled with the
tool call or `A<n>` action. Yantra geometry — the concentric square-in-circle around a center
point — appears only as restrained structure: the logo mark, the contract ring, the Bindu. No
literal religious iconography.

### The five rules

1. **Glass for controls, paper for content.** Floating controls over the live browser are glass.
   Briefs, tables, logs and forms sit on solid surfaces so their contrast never depends on what
   is behind them.
2. **Color is spent on meaning.** Grays carry all structure. A saturated hue appears only when it
   says something: act here, this passed, this needs you.
3. **Three voices.** The user writes in plain sans. The agent's reading of the goal is set in
   italic. The engine speaks in mono: tool calls, refs, URLs, verified values.
4. **Every action has a CLI twin.** Each action can show and copy the exact `yantra` command it
   runs; the palette accepts that same syntax.
5. **Evidence before eloquence.** A claim shows its citation, a requirement its proof, a protected
   value only the fact that it was protected.

### Color: fog and signal

All colors are defined in **OKLCH**, which keeps lightness steps perceptually even and lets one
hue be re-lit per theme without drifting.

**Fog ramp** — thirteen neutrals at hue 255, chroma 0.002–0.011, tinted slightly cool so nothing
reads as a dead mid-gray:

| Token    | Name     | OKLCH             | Default role             |
| -------- | -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------ |
| `fog-00` | Paper    | `0.994 0.002 255` | Light surface            |
| `fog-05` | Frost    | `0.975 0.004 255` | Light page background    |
| `fog-10` | Fog      | `0.952 0.005 255` | Light sunken / wells     |
| `fog-20` | Mist     | `0.915 0.006 255` | Light hairline           |
| `fog-30` | Haze     | `0.862 0.007 255` | Light strong rule        |
| `fog-40` | Pewter   | `0.760 0.009 255` | Dark secondary ink       |
| `fog-50` | Slate    | `0.640 0.010 255` | Dark tertiary ink        |
| `fog-60` | Steel    | `0.530 0.011 255` | Light tertiary ink       |
| `fog-70` | Graphite | `0.420 0.011 255` | Light secondary ink      |
| `fog-80` | Carbon   | `0.310 0.010 255` | Dark strong rule         |
| `fog-90` | Ink      | `0.220 0.009 255` | —                        |
| `fog-95` | Void     | `0.165 0.008 255` | Light ink / dark surface |
| `fog-99` | Abyss    | `0.125 0.007 255` | Dark page background     |

**Signals** — five saturated hues, each with exactly one job. Every signal pairs with a shape
(icon or glyph) so state survives grayscale and color-vision deficiency.

| Signal           | Job                                                                                       | Light (OKLCH)                                               | Dark (OKLCH)                                                          | Shape              |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| **Ion** (accent) | Act and live: primary buttons, focus ring, the element the engine is touching, live state | fill `0.55 0.14 218`, text on it white; ink `0.50 0.12 218` | fill `0.80 0.14 218`, text on it `0.18 0.03 230`; ink `0.82 0.12 218` | —                  |
| **Jade**         | Fulfilled, verified, requirement met with a citation                                      | `0.55 0.13 162`                                             | `0.76 0.14 162`                                                       | circle-check       |
| **Amber**        | Partial, unverified, budget running low, steer                                            | `0.62 0.15 65`                                              | `0.80 0.14 65`                                                        | half-filled circle |
| **Crimson**      | Failed, violated, blocked by site or policy                                               | `0.55 0.20 25`                                              | `0.70 0.18 25`                                                        | circle-x           |
| **Rani**         | Needs you: consent, handoff, a question only the user can answer                          | `0.55 0.22 352`                                             | `0.72 0.20 352`                                                       | hand               |

`Aborted` deliberately has **no** signal color (secondary ink plus a ban glyph): the user stopped
it, so nothing is wrong and nothing needs attention.

**Why Ion.** It is the most futuristic of the three studied directions (HUD cyan), and it stays
clear of the current AI-product palette (purple gradients) and of the two looks the study
rejected as generated-design clichés (vermilion or acid green on near-black). Its known weakness —
weaker on light paper — is handled by giving Ion **two fills**: a deeper fill with white text in
light theme, a bright fill with near-black text in dark theme. Both must pass 4.5:1 in CI. Ion
also sits well away from Jade (218° vs 162°), so action and success never blur together. Ion is at
its best in dark theme, so the Mission surface is designed dark-first, but both themes are
first-class and the default follows the OS.

**Token tiers (Tailwind v4 `@theme`).**

1. **Primitive** — `--color-fog-*`, `--color-ion-*`, `--color-jade-*` …: raw ramps; never used by
   components.
2. **Semantic** — `--color-bg`, `--color-surface`, `--color-sunken`, `--color-ink`,
   `--color-ink-2`, `--color-ink-3`, `--color-rule`, `--color-rule-strong`, `--color-accent`,
   `--color-on-accent`, `--color-accent-ink`, `--color-signal-{fulfilled,partial,failed,needs-you}`,
   `--color-glass-{tint,edge,spec}`: what components use. Tailwind v4 generates utilities
   (`bg-surface`, `text-ink-2`, `border-rule`) from these.
3. **Component** — `--button-*`, `--hud-*`, `--ring-*` where a component needs a local knob.

Themes switch by redefining the semantic tier under `prefers-color-scheme` and an explicit
`data-theme` attribute (the study's exact pattern). **A raw palette utility or hex value in a
component is a bug** — enforced by lint, the same way "a site name in code is a bug" is enforced
in the engine.

### Glass

- **Recipe**: semantic tint at 66% (light) / 72% (dark) opacity, `backdrop-filter: blur(20px)
saturate(1.5)`, a faint fractal-noise texture to prevent banding, a 1 px edge, and a 1 px inner
  specular highlight on the top edge. Dark glass uses a higher tint floor because dark glass over
  bright web pages loses contrast fastest.
- **Where glass is allowed**: HUD panels over the live viewport, the command palette, popovers,
  toasts, sheets over the viewport. Nowhere else.
- **Solid mode**: a preference (`ui.surfaces: glass | solid`) that swaps every glass surface for
  solid surface plus strong rule. `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce` forces it. The app also
  falls back to Solid automatically if frame time over the viewport exceeds budget.
- **Scrim floor**: the minimum tint opacity is a token, raised automatically when the contrast
  sampler measures a busy backdrop.

### Typography: three voices

| Voice            | Face                             | Setting                                                            | Used for                                                                 |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Display / labels | **Archivo** (variable, OFL)      | width 112–125%, weight 600–700, uppercase with tracking for labels | Mode names, section labels, the wordmark, large numerals                 |
| Human / reading  | **Archivo**                      | width 100%, weight 400–600                                         | Everything the user writes and reads, Brief prose                        |
| Agent            | **Archivo Italic**               | width 100%, secondary ink                                          | The contract's "understood:" summary and revisions                       |
| Engine           | **Martian Mono** (variable, OFL) | width 87.5%, weight 400–600                                        | Tool calls, refs (`#07`, `A6`), URLs, IDs, verified values, the CLI twin |

One family at several widths gives hierarchy without a font zoo; the expanded width gives the
instrument-panel feel without Eurostile kitsch. **Fonts are self-hosted** (bundled with the app,
e.g. via Fontsource packages): a local-first app makes no third-party requests, works offline,
and does not tell a font CDN when you open it. Tabular numerals are on wherever digits align.

Scale (rem): 0.72 · 0.8125 · 0.9375 · 1.125 · 1.5 · 2.25 · 4.1 (display clamp).

### Iconography

- **Lucide** (`lucide-react`, ISC) at stroke 1.75 on 16–20 px.
- Components never import Lucide directly. They import from a **semantic icon registry**
  (`icon.outcome.fulfilled`, `icon.action.stop`, `icon.status.needsYou`), so the icon set can be
  swapped or retuned in one file.
- A small set of **custom glyphs** drawn on Lucide's own 24 px grid and stroke rules so they are
  indistinguishable: bindu, contract, capture, handoff, protected, provenance.

### Shape, space and elevation

- **Radius**: 4 (chips, badges), 8 (controls, plates), 14 (the cockpit frame). No `rounded-2xl`
  everywhere.
- **Space**: 4 px base. Two densities, **Comfort** and **Compact**, are a token multiplier, not
  separate components (`ui.density` preference).
- **Elevation by luminance and hairlines**, not drop shadows. Shadows exist only under glass, to
  separate it from the moving viewport.

### Motion

Motion means something or it does not exist.

- **Bindu** states: idle (hollow), thinking (slow breathe), acting (ring pulse), needs you (fast
  Rani pulse), fulfilled (solid Jade).
- **Target lock**: brackets tighten once on the touched element.
- **Requirement tick**: a ring segment fills when evidence arrives.
- **View Transitions** for structural changes: a finished run's HUD morphs into its Brief; route
  changes cross-fade.
- Durations 120 / 200 / 320 ms. `prefers-reduced-motion` stops all loops. No decorative loops
  besides the Bindu, no parallax, no animated gradients.

### Instruments: components only Yantra has

Each instrument is typed by a `@yantra/protocol` shape, which is what makes parity enforceable.

| Instrument                         | Renders                                                                                                 | Protocol source                                                              |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `OutcomeBadge`                     | fulfilled / partial / handoff / failed / aborted with counts                                            | `task_outcome` (FEAT-054)                                                    |
| `ContractRing` + `RequirementList` | one ring segment per requirement; status, citations, revision                                           | `contract.json` revisions; Brief requirements and constraints (FEAT-052/053) |
| `CitationChip` + `EvidencePane`    | `[n]` chips that open the quoted snippet, host, fetch time                                              | Brief `sources`, citation verdicts                                           |
| `ConditionTable`                   | verified / violated / unverified rows, cited rows, "also consulted"                                     | Brief `constraints`, `facets` (FEAT-053)                                     |
| `RunTimeline`                      | live tool-call log, steers, escalations, recovery verdicts                                              | tool-call and runtime events (FEAT-034/048/059)                              |
| `BudgetGauge`                      | hops, sources, wall clock, model calls, captures                                                        | `run-health.json` budgets, research budgets                                  |
| `GuardedSwitch`                    | hold-to-confirm consent card; Deny is default; timeout shown                                            | `ConfirmationRequest` (FEAT-019)                                             |
| `ProtectedValue`                   | hatched field, "never leaves the page", the `${secret:…}` reference — never the value, never its length | secret refs, protected-value withholding (FEAT-056)                          |
| `BrowserViewport`                  | live screencast, target brackets, blanking on protected screens                                         | task page screencast + action evidence (FEAT-060)                            |
| `ProvenanceThread`                 | how a URL was attested: goal → search → page → link                                                     | `provenance: {match, kind, via, link_kind}` (FEAT-051)                       |
| `CaptureGallery`                   | saved captures vs images the model saw, parts, incomplete labels                                        | `screenshots/`, `capture-*` (FEAT-036/058)                                   |
| `HealthCheck`                      | doctor rows with remediation command                                                                    | `yantra doctor --json` checks                                                |
| `Bindu`                            | engine state everywhere in the app                                                                      | run lifecycle + pending confirmations                                        |
| `CliTwin`                          | the command a UI action runs, copyable                                                                  | command registry invocation                                                  |
| `EventInspector`                   | any event or artifact with no bespoke instrument, as a typed key/value tree                             | the fallback that guarantees day-one visibility                              |

### Banned patterns

Purple-to-blue gradients · a sparkle icon for "AI" · chat bubbles as the primary metaphor · emoji
in UI · rows of KPI tiles · `rounded-2xl` and drop shadows on every block · vermilion or acid
green on near-black · Inter or Space Grotesk as the default face · glass behind running text ·
status by color alone · a control that does nothing for the current command.

## Information Architecture & Surface Map

### Surfaces

| Surface       | Purpose                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Mission**   | Composer (mode: Ask / Research / Do / Run, options generated per command) and the live cockpit for the running task          |
| **Ledger**    | All runs: outcome, mode, goal, duration, cost; filters; resume; open                                                         |
| **Brief**     | Reading view of a finished run's Brief or template document, with conditions, citations, evidence pane, captures, exports    |
| **Audit**     | Trust narrative, model-bound payloads, what stayed local, provenance threads, secret usage                                   |
| **Workflows** | Saved workflows: natural-language YAML view, lint, params, run, schedule                                                     |
| **Templates** | Report templates: slots, guidance, lint, preview                                                                             |
| **Schedules** | Registered schedules, next fires, parked runs, daemon status                                                                 |
| **Inbox**     | Everything waiting on the user: confirmations, handoffs, parked scheduled runs                                               |
| **Settings**  | Installation (`config.yaml`), Preferences (`profile.yaml`), Models, Credentials (write-only), Browser, Sites, Data directory |
| **Health**    | `doctor` checks with one-click remediation where an engineered path exists                                                   |
| **Usage**     | Task count, tokens and cost by type and period                                                                               |

The Session 1 principle "one box, one feed" survives as **one composer**: there is exactly one
place to start work. It no longer means one screen.

### CLI → app parity map (current commands)

"Generated" means the MVP surface is a form or table generated from the command registry and the
command's `--json` output schema, styled by Drshya but without bespoke layout. Bespoke design
replaces it in the phase listed.

| CLI command                                        | App surface                                            | MVP                                              | Bespoke in       |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- |
| `ask`, `research`, `do`                            | Mission composer + cockpit; Brief                      | Bespoke                                          | MVP              |
| `run`                                              | Mission (Run mode) + Workflows                         | Bespoke cockpit, generated params                | Phase 2          |
| `resume`                                           | Ledger row action → Mission                            | Bespoke                                          | MVP              |
| `list`                                             | Ledger                                                 | Bespoke                                          | MVP              |
| `show`                                             | Ledger detail / Workflows detail                       | Bespoke                                          | MVP              |
| `open`                                             | Brief (in-app); "open file" action                     | Bespoke                                          | MVP              |
| `report`                                           | Audit → Report tab                                     | Bespoke                                          | MVP              |
| `audit`                                            | Audit                                                  | Bespoke                                          | MVP              |
| `lint`                                             | Workflows → Lint panel                                 | Generated                                        | Phase 2          |
| `usage`                                            | Usage                                                  | Generated table                                  | Phase 2 (charts) |
| `init`                                             | First-run onboarding                                   | Bespoke                                          | MVP              |
| `doctor`                                           | Health                                                 | Bespoke                                          | MVP              |
| `config path/list/get/set/unset/validate/data-dir` | Settings → Installation, Data                          | Generated                                        | Phase 2          |
| `config edit`                                      | Settings → Installation → raw YAML with validate       | Generated                                        | Phase 2          |
| `prefs`, `profile`                                 | Settings → Preferences (with provenance)               | Generated                                        | Phase 2          |
| `secret set/list/rm`                               | Settings → Credentials (names only; set is write-only) | Bespoke (security)                               | MVP              |
| `model list/add/rm/default`                        | Settings → Models                                      | Generated                                        | Phase 2          |
| `browser install/list/use/check/update`            | Settings → Browser                                     | Generated (install/update keep explicit consent) | Phase 2          |
| `sites list/add/remove`                            | Settings → Sites                                       | Generated                                        | Phase 2          |
| `template new/lint/save/list/show/remove`          | Templates                                              | Generated                                        | Phase 2          |
| `schedule`, `schedules`, `unschedule`              | Schedules                                              | Generated                                        | Phase 2          |
| `confirm`                                          | Inbox + `GuardedSwitch`                                | Bespoke                                          | MVP              |
| `daemon start/stop/status`                         | Health → Daemon (stop asks, then closes the app)       | Generated                                        | —                |

**Exemptions** (written into the parity manifest with reasons): `--json` (the app is structured
by nature), `--open` (the app is the viewer), `--print` on `open` (shown as "Copy path").

**Not yet a command:** the recorder (FEAT-008, with FEAT-042/043 lifecycle work) exists in core
but has no `yantra record` command. When it gets one, the parity test will force an app surface;
the intended design is "Record" mode in Workflows (visible Chrome with overlay → annotate review).

**Option applicability is inherited, not re-decided.** Per memory, a flag is registered only on
commands that can act on it (`--no-browse` on `research` only; `--turn-timeout` on `do` only). The
composer's option panel is generated from the same registry, so the app cannot show a dead
control, and precedence (flag > env > preference > default) is displayed with its source.

---

## Architecture

### Shape

```
 yantra ui ──► Chrome --app=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/launch#<code>   (dedicated UI profile)
                    │
                    │  HTTPS-less localhost: static app + launch exchange + artifact files (HTTP)
                    │  commands, subscriptions, live events (WebSocket, JSON-RPC 2.0)
                    │  screencast frames (separate binary WebSocket)
                    ▼
            yantra daemon  (FEAT-021 scheduler + new app server; single-instance lock)
                    │  same executor the CLI uses: RunOrchestrator, agent runtime, ConnectorIO
                    ▼
     @yantra/core · @yantra/agent · <data-dir>/runs/<id>/ · index.db
                    ▲
 yantra <cmd> ──────┘  CLI keeps running inline, unchanged; writes the same runs/ and index
```

New and changed packages:

- **`packages/ui`** — Drshya (published name `@yantra/ui`; brand name Drshya). Depends on
  `@yantra/protocol` for types only. Never imports core.
- **`apps/web`** — the app. Depends on `@yantra/ui`, `@yantra/protocol` and a thin transport client.
- **Daemon server** — added to the existing daemon. Contains adaptation only: no business logic
  that the CLI path does not also run.
- **`@yantra/protocol`** — gains the command registry contract, the unified run-event union, the
  app-facing transport messages, and a new `decided_by` variant.

### The run-event stream (main prerequisite)

Live information is spread across stderr lines, `--json` events (`agent_progress`,
`capability_gap`), `runtime.jsonl`, `tool-calls.jsonl` and `events.jsonl`. The app needs **one
versioned, Zod-defined `RunEvent` union** emitted through `ConnectorIO`. The CLI's terminal and
JSON renderers become two more consumers of the same stream, which makes the CLI's own output
more consistent too. Yantra is pre-release, so the internal event shapes can break cleanly
(memory), but persisted run artifacts must remain readable.

### Read side first

The run directory is already a complete, durable record. The daemon can serve the Ledger, Brief,
Audit (reusing `audit-builder`) and captures from `runs/` and `index.db` without any live-execution
plumbing. This is why the read-side surfaces are the first shippable slice: they exercise the design
system against real data before the run-event stream exists.

### Consent from the app

`ConfirmationDecidedBy` is a closed enum (`user_interactive | user_cli_confirm | timeout`) with no
agent variant, by design. The app needs a fourth human-originated variant, proposed
**`user_app`**, produced only by the app's `ConnectorIO` gateway after the hold gesture
completes. Type-level unforgeability is preserved. Parked scheduled runs (the daemon's
park-and-notify gateway) appear in the Inbox, and `yantra confirm` and the Inbox resolve the same
parked records, so the two can never disagree.

### Live browser viewport

- CDP `Page.startScreencast` on the **task page only** (never the FEAT-050 background pool pages),
  JPEG, size-capped, frame-acked so a slow app throttles the stream instead of queueing.
- Frames go only to subscribed app sessions. They are **never persisted and never sent to the
  model**, so they are not "screenshots" under the `context.screenshots` grant — the same as
  watching a headed browser window. This should still be stated in the safety docs.
- When the **sensitive-screen latch** is set, the daemon stops forwarding frames (server-side,
  not a client blur) and the viewport shows "Protected screen — hidden".
- **Headed runs** show "Running in a visible window" with a focus action instead of a stream.
- **Target brackets** need element boxes on action evidence. FEAT-060 action evidence is
  value-free identity; adding a viewport-relative box is a protocol addition (open question).

### Localhost security

Any web page the user visits can send requests to `127.0.0.1`. The server therefore:

- binds `127.0.0.1` only, on a random port, recorded in the daemon lock;
- issues a one-time **launch code** to `yantra ui`, passed in the URL fragment (never sent in a
  request line or logged), exchanged once for an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` session cookie;
- requires `Host` to be `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>` (defeats DNS rebinding) and an
  exact `Origin` on every mutation and WebSocket upgrade;
- serves no CORS headers;
- treats credentials as **write-only**: the app can set or remove `secret` entries and list names,
  never read values; a canary-secret test scans every response and frame header;
- serves artifact files (captures, screenshots) only to an authenticated session, with
  `Content-Type` fixed by extension and `Content-Security-Policy` on the app.

### Parity mechanism

1. **Command registry.** Extract the commander definitions into a declarative registry
   (commands, options with type, default, precedence chain, applicability, exit codes, `--json`
   output schema). The CLI builds commander from it; the app builds the composer, generated
   forms and the palette parser from it. A snapshot of every `--help` output proves the
   extraction changed nothing for the CLI.
2. **Parity manifest.** `apps/web` maps every registry entry to a surface or an exemption with a
   reason. A test enumerates the registry and fails on anything unmapped.
3. **Event exhaustiveness.** Instruments switch over the `RunEvent` union with compile-time
   exhaustiveness; anything without a bespoke instrument is explicitly routed to `EventInspector`.
4. **Artifact registry.** Each run-artifact file type maps to a viewer; unknown files fall back to
   a raw viewer (JSON tree, text, image).
5. **CLI twin.** Every app mutation is a `CommandInvocation` (command + argv) sent to the daemon.
   The same object renders as a copyable shell command, and the palette parses typed argv with the
   same registry.

### Library architecture

```
apps/web            surfaces: routes, layout, data loading (TanStack Router + Query)
  └─ @yantra/ui     instruments  → typed by @yantra/protocol
                    primitives   → react-aria-components + tailwind-variants
                    icons        → semantic registry over lucide-react + custom glyphs
                    tokens       → drshya.css (Tailwind v4 @theme), themes, densities
```

- Each layer imports only from the layer below. Surfaces never use a raw color; instruments never
  parse a raw event.
- Primitives are styled through React Aria's state data attributes (`data-hovered`,
  `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-selected`) using the
  `tailwindcss-react-aria-components` plugin, with `tailwind-variants` for multi-slot variants.
- A **gallery** renders every primitive and instrument in both themes, both densities and Solid
  mode, backed by Playwright screenshot tests.

## Features

### MVP Features (Phase 1)

The MVP in one sentence: **the Drshya design system, a secure local app opened by `yantra ui`,
read surfaces for every run, a live cockpit for `ask`/`research`/`do`, and a parity framework that
gives every other command at least a generated surface.**

- **Drshya design system (`packages/ui`)**: Tokens (fog, signals with Ion, glass, type, space,
  radius, motion) in Tailwind v4 `@theme`; React Aria primitives (Button, Field, Select,
  ComboBox, Dialog, Popover, Menu, Tabs, Table with virtualization, Toast, Tooltip); the semantic
  icon registry; the MVP instruments (OutcomeBadge, ContractRing, RequirementList, CitationChip,
  EvidencePane, ConditionTable, RunTimeline, BudgetGauge, GuardedSwitch, ProtectedValue, Bindu,
  CliTwin, EventInspector); lint rules banning raw colors; gallery with visual-regression
  snapshots. Everything else depends on this, and building it first against real run data keeps the
  look honest.
- **Local app server and `yantra ui`**: The daemon serves the static app, the launch-code
  exchange, a JSON-RPC WebSocket and authenticated artifact files on `127.0.0.1`. `yantra ui`
  starts the daemon if needed and opens Chrome in `--app` mode with a dedicated profile kept apart
  from every automation profile; `--print` prints the URL instead (same spelling as `open
--print`). Includes the full localhost security suite.
- **Ledger, Brief and Audit (read side)**: Runs list from `index.db` plus the file scan, Brief
  reader with conditions, cited rows, evidence pane and captures, Audit with trust narrative and
  model-bound versus local-only material. Ships before live execution and proves the design
  system on real artifacts.
- **Mission: composer and live cockpit for `ask`, `research`, `do`**: Composer with mode and
  options generated from the registry; the `RunEvent` stream; the glass HUD (contract ring,
  engine log, budgets, Bindu, CLI twin); consent through `GuardedSwitch` with the new `user_app`
  provenance; the live `BrowserViewport` with sensitive-screen blanking; the Inbox for pending
  confirmations; a Brief morph on completion; `resume` from the Ledger. This is the "whoa" moment
  and the reason the app exists.
- **Parity framework and generated surfaces**: Command registry extraction, parity manifest test,
  artifact registry, palette that accepts CLI syntax; generated Drshya forms and tables for every
  remaining command (config, prefs/profile, model, browser, sites, template, schedule, usage,
  daemon); bespoke onboarding (`init`), Health (`doctor`) and Credentials (`secret`). After this, no
  CLI feature is invisible in the app.

### Phase 2 Features (Post-MVP)

- **Workflow studio**: Natural-language YAML view with inline lint, params form, run and schedule,
  review of `do --save-as` output, locator-candidate inspection. — _Deferred because: the generated
  surface covers the commands; a studio is a large design project best done after the cockpit
  proves the language._
- **Recorder and annotate in the app**: "Record" mode (visible Chrome with overlay) ending in a
  web annotate review that replaces the CLI prompts (TODO: "Web UI for annotation"). — _Deferred
  because: the recorder has no CLI command yet; parity will force this when it does._
- **Schedules and Inbox, bespoke**: Timeline of next fires, parked runs, desktop notifications
  from the app window for things that need the user. — _Deferred because: generated surfaces plus
  the MVP Inbox cover the function._
- **Template editor**: Slots and model-only guidance with live preview of `document.md`. —
  _Deferred because: low frequency, high design effort._
- **Usage and cost charts**: Per-workflow cost trend and per-provider comparison (TODO Phase 2
  token-usage visibility). — _Deferred because: data exists; presentation is not urgent._
- **Provenance thread view**: Visual attestation chains for every URL a run touched. — _Deferred
  because: Audit lists provenance as text in MVP; the graph view is an enhancement._
- **Attach to CLI-launched runs**: Watch a run started in a terminal live in the app. —
  _Deferred because: needs the CLI to publish events to a running daemon (open question)._
- **Compact density and keyboard map**: Full shortcut sheet and compact density across every
  surface. — _Deferred because: Comfort density first; Compact is a token multiplier once
  layouts settle._

### Parked Ideas

- **Tauri or Electron shell**: The Chrome app window gives a desktop feel at zero extra weight
  using the browser Yantra already manages. Revisit only for OS integration a browser window
  cannot provide (tray icon, global hotkey, start at login).
- **Remote or multi-user web app**: Needs a real auth model and the remote `BrowserProvider`;
  stays with the platform doc's Phase 3+.
- **Mobile companion**: Phone is a poor host (platform doc); approvals by notification could come
  through a connector instead.
- **Publishing Drshya as a public package**: Interesting for the brand, but only once the API is
  stable.
- **Brief instruments inside VS Code** (webview reuse of Drshya): Parked with the platform doc's
  IDE-extension idea.
- **3D or WebGL effects**: Decoration, against rule 2.
- **User theming / theme marketplace**: Two themes, two densities, glass or solid. That is the
  whole customization surface.

---

## Platform & Distribution

- **Platform**: Windows, macOS, Linux — wherever the CLI runs. The app runs in Chromium only: the
  same browser resolution as tasks (FEAT-043–045), but always a **separate** window and profile
  from any automation browser. Targeting evergreen Chromium lets Drshya use OKLCH,
  `backdrop-filter`, container queries, the Popover API, anchor positioning and View Transitions
  without fallbacks.
- **Distribution**: `apps/web` is built to static files and shipped inside the CLI package; the
  daemon serves them. No separate download, no separate update channel.
- **Deployment model**: Local only, `127.0.0.1`. The daemon still does not start at login; it
  starts when the user runs `yantra ui` or `yantra daemon start`.

## Technology Direction

- **Recommended approach**: A token-driven design system package (Drshya) consumed by a thin
  React app, hosted by the existing daemon, held to the CLI by a shared command registry and a
  single run-event protocol. All behavior stays in core; the server adapts and the app renders.
- **Key technology leanings**:
  - **Tailwind CSS v4.3** with CSS-first `@theme` (three token tiers) — tokens are a CSS file,
    themes are selector blocks, and utilities are generated from semantic tokens only.
  - **React 19 + Vite + TanStack Router** (the Session 1 direction, confirmed) and
    **TanStack Query** for read-side caching; a small external store (`useSyncExternalStore`) for
    live streams. Planner to confirm the store.
  - **React Aria Components** — the broadest accessible primitive set (virtualized Table and
    GridList, Tree, drag and drop for workflow steps, DatePicker and Calendar for schedules),
    built-in i18n, and state exposed as data attributes that style naturally with Tailwind. Bundle
    size is irrelevant on localhost.
  - **tailwind-variants** (with `tailwind-merge`) for multi-slot component variants.
  - **lucide-react** behind the semantic icon registry.
  - **Archivo** and **Martian Mono**, self-hosted.
  - **Motion** (motion.dev) only where CSS and View Transitions cannot express the animation.
  - **JSON-RPC 2.0 over WebSocket** (Session 1 transport, now real) plus a binary WebSocket for
    screencast frames.
  - **Zod** remains the source of truth for every message the app sends or receives.
- **Technologies explicitly avoided**:
  - **shadcn/ui's visual layer** — the signature of generated apps; we keep only the
    code-ownership idea.
  - **Pre-styled kits** (MUI, Chakra, Mantine, DaisyUI) — they would be the design language.
  - **Runtime CSS-in-JS** (Emotion, styled-components) — tokens live in CSS.
  - **Next.js** — still no SSR need for a localhost app.
  - **Tauri / Electron** for now — see Parked Ideas.
  - **Google Fonts or any CDN at runtime** — local-first means no third-party requests.
  - **Chat UI kits** — Yantra is not a chat.
- **Relevant trends**:
  - **Glass is back and contested**: Liquid Glass made translucency mainstream in 2025 and drew a
    legibility backlash. The lesson is encoded in rule 1 and Solid mode.
  - **Headless primitives + own styling** is now the standard for serious design systems. Base UI
    reached 1.0 in 2026 and shadcn/ui now supports it alongside Radix; React Aria leads on breadth
    and i18n.
  - **OKLCH tokens** have replaced HSL ramps in modern systems (Tailwind v4's default palette is
    OKLCH).
  - **Agent live views** are becoming expected; none yet treat the agent's understanding, actions
    and the user's authority as separate instruments.
  - **Command palettes** are the power-user baseline (Linear, Raycast, VS Code).

## UX / Developer Experience Considerations

- **Keyboard first.** `Ctrl/Cmd+K` palette reaches every action and accepts CLI syntax; every
  surface has shortcuts; focus is always visible (Ion ring).
- **Calm by default, deep on demand.** Priya sees the composer, the contract summary and the
  Brief; the Engine panel and budgets are one keystroke away and remembered per user.
- **Honest words.** Outcome words, condition statuses and failure reasons are the CLI's words,
  verbatim. Nothing turns Jade unless it is fulfilled or verified.
- **Errors carry the fix.** Every error names what happened and offers the engineered remedy (the
  `doctor` hint, the exact CLI command), and never a remedy the engine has no path for (memory:
  advice may only name a move the engine can perform).
- **Preferences live where preferences live.** Theme, density and glass/solid are `profile.yaml`
  keys (`ui.theme`, `ui.density`, `ui.surfaces`), settable from the app or `yantra prefs set`,
  not hidden in browser storage — the `config.yaml` / `profile.yaml` ownership rule applies to the
  app too.
- **Agent-optional.** With no provider configured, `do` shows why it is unavailable and the fix;
  `ask` and `research` run deterministically; replay works.
- **Accessible.** WCAG 2.2 AA, React Aria semantics, color plus shape for every state, reduced
  motion and reduced transparency honored.
- **No engagement mechanics.** Inherited from the platform doc: no streaks, no weekly summaries.
  The only notifications are things that need the user.

---

## Risks & Open Questions

### Known Risks

- **Registry extraction is a cross-cutting refactor** (about 30 commands, 98 options). →
  _Mitigation: migrate command by command; the registry builds commander; a `--help` snapshot
  suite proves no CLI change; parity test tolerates "not yet migrated" only behind a dated
  allowlist._
- **Glass over a live screencast may cost too much GPU or lose legibility.** → _Mitigation: a
  one-week spike before the cockpit is built (5–10 fps under four blurred panels, measured frame
  time and sampled contrast); automatic Solid fallback over budget; Solid preference always
  available._
- **Localhost attack surface.** → _Mitigation: the security model above, plus its test suite as a
  merge gate; launch code single-use; Host/Origin checks on every request and upgrade._
- **Ion is weak on light paper.** → _Mitigation: two fills and a darker ink variant; automated
  contrast checks for every accent pairing in both themes._
- **Two execution hosts (inline CLI and daemon) could diverge.** → _Mitigation: both call the same
  core orchestrator through `ConnectorIO`; server routes contain adaptation only; shared e2e
  scenarios run through both hosts._
- **Design-system perfectionism delays usefulness.** → _Mitigation: read-side surfaces ship first
  on a partial Drshya; generated surfaces give every command a usable view before bespoke work._
- **Screencast privacy.** → _Mitigation: task page only, never persisted, never to the model,
  frames dropped server-side under the sensitive-screen latch; documented in Safety and Privacy._
- **Daemon crash ends app-launched runs.** → _Mitigation: existing checkpoint and `resume`; the app
  shows a reconnect state and offers resume from the Ledger._
- **Licensing.** Archivo (OFL), Martian Mono (OFL), Lucide (ISC), React Aria (Apache-2.0),
  Tailwind (MIT) are all compatible with Yantra's Apache-2.0; record them in `NOTICE`.

### Open Questions for Planner

- **Run-event union scope.** Which of `agent_progress`, `capability_gap`, runtime events, tool-call
  phases and `events.jsonl` kinds fold into one `RunEvent` union, and do persisted JSONL files keep
  their current shapes (recommended) or become serializations of the union?
- **Transport detail.** JSON-RPC 2.0 over WebSocket for commands and subscriptions (recommended,
  matches Session 1) versus HTTP + Server-Sent Events. Screencast on a separate binary socket
  either way.
- **Command registry design.** Own declarative format that generates commander, or annotate the
  existing commander definitions and derive the registry from them? The first is cleaner; the
  second is a smaller diff.
- **Live view of CLI-launched runs.** Should a CLI run publish to a running daemon (opt-in
  attach), or should the app tail `runtime.jsonl` and `tool-calls.jsonl`? Affects Phase 2 only.
- **Target-bracket geometry.** Add a viewport-relative bounding box to `A<n>` action evidence
  (value-free, so FEAT-056 still holds)? Without it the viewport shows the stream but no brackets.
- **`decided_by` variant name.** `user_app` (proposed) — confirm, and decide whether parked-run
  resolution from the Inbox also uses it or keeps `user_cli_confirm` semantics.
- **Gallery tool.** Storybook, Ladle, or an in-app `/gallery` route behind a dev flag. Needs
  Playwright screenshot integration either way.
- **Package naming.** `@yantra/ui` with "Drshya" as the brand (recommended), or `@yantra/drshya`.
  The common English transliteration is "Drishya"; the user chose "Drshya", which this doc uses.
- **Daemon lifetime.** Does `yantra ui` leave the daemon running after the window closes (needed
  for schedules), and how does the app show that?
- **Chrome app-mode behavior on each OS.** Window identity, taskbar/dock icon and profile
  location under `~/.yantra`, so the UI window is never mistaken for an automation browser.

## Assumptions

- The app host is Chromium; the user has, or Yantra manages, a Chrome that supports `--app`.
- Single user on a single machine; no multi-user auth.
- The scheduler daemon can host interactive runs as well (it already runs the inline executor).
- Yantra is pre-release: internal interfaces may break cleanly, persisted artifact formats stay
  readable (memory).
- English UI strings first; React Aria's i18n keeps localization possible later.
- Archivo and Martian Mono variable fonts cover the needed widths and weights when self-hosted.
